result.title: Through a PRISM, Clearly: Step-Sequence Reasoning for Mistake Recognition in Procedural Videos
result.summary: Procedural mistake recognition requires identifying deviations from valid multi-step activities. We study post-completion recognition from videos with benchmark-provided step boundaries. We introduce PRISM (Procedural mistake Recognition via Interpretable Semantic Modeling), which grounds video segments in language and maps their descriptions to procedural states using a lightweight hidden Markov model trained on correct executions. Reference alignment and semantic checks identify errors in step content and order. To support evaluation across heterogeneous benchmarks, we map dataset-specific annotations to four edit-based error types: insertion, deletion, substitution, and transposition. Across three benchmarks, we compare gold and VLM-generated descriptions in raw, semantic-role, and action-object forms. Decoder controls show consistent gains from the trained local decoder over nearest-candidate matching, with additional, dataset-dependent benefits from sequence decoding. Semantic role labeling improves Any-F1 in all six matched grounded comparisons, although the gains vary across datasets and do not translate into uniform improvements under separate configuration selection. These results establish language grounding as an effective interface for explicit procedural mistake reasoning and characterize the contributions of representation and decoding.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 PRISM：把视频步骤片段转成语言描述，用轻量 HMM 建模正确执行流程，通过参考对齐与语义检查识别插入、删除、替换、换位类错误，并在三个基准上比较 gold 与 VLM 描述的不同语义表示及解码方式。
AI.relevance_reason: 「接地描述→隐状态序列→序列解码」这一管线和它对描述表示形式、局部解码器相对最近候选匹配的消融，可供核查 LVR 中推理状态表示与更新方式；但研究对象是视频步骤错误识别，而非 VLM 内部 latent 推理。
